links.reason: Devanthi's cause (ஒருநோன்பு பொய்த்தாய் பழம்பிறப்பில், 55-56) explains Kannaki's present separation, while the goddess's curse (பட்டனிர், 170, plural, on both of them) explains the killing, so the two are not incompatible claims about one ruin. Nor does the goddess's speech set Devanthi's guess aside; the note also narrows the curse to Kovalan when பட்டனிர் includes Kannaki.

Kural 314 treats those who hurt oneself (இன்னாசெய் தாரை), and 550 the king's dealing with murderers (கொலையிற் கொடியாரை வேந்து); different advice for different situations is not a tension. The shared verb ஒறுத்தல் does mark a real person/state contrast, but teaches only restates that the word is shared.

Line 21 வளம்தலை மயங்கிய நனந்தலை மறுகும் is Pattinappaalai 193 word for word, and 18-19 (துகிரும் ஆரமும் அகிலும் ... முத்தும் மணியும் பொன்னும்) repeat the older poem's goods (187-189). So in the epic too the line closes a list of goods, not a census of craftsmen, and teaches misplaces it. The other-side gain is generic.

Neelakesi's சருவம் துக்கம் parody gives no cause, while Manimekalai 186-187 (துன்பம் தோற்றம் பற்றே காரணம், இன்பம் வீடே பற்றிலி காரணம்) ties sorrow to clinging. That contrast is real. But the Manimekalai unit never states 'all is suffering', so this is a polemic against a doctrine, not two incompatible claims about one thing.

Both units rest a courtesan line's art on a dancer's fall before Indra: Silappathikaram 6:20-24 (ஆயிரம் கண்ணோன் ... உருப்பசி நல்காள் ... சாபம் பெற்ற மங்கை மாதவி வழிமுதல்) and Manimekalai 24:13-14 (தேவர் கோன் தன் முன் உருப்பசி முனிந்த என் குலத்து ஒருத்தியும்). Chithirapathi uses that heavenly charter to measure the shame of the begging bowl (யான் உறு துன்பம் யாவரும் பட்டிலர், 17; 21-23), so the pairing does show the myth turned from certificate into yardstick.

Both units do describe the Sankhya self as one knowing awareness (Manimekalai 230-232 ஒன்றாய் ... உணர்வாய் ... புருடன்; Neelakesi 780 பரமாத்துமன், துய்த்தலும் காண்டலும்), and Neelakesi answers that souls (சீவன்கட்கு) have that knowledge. But the Manimekalai only reports the view, so the opposition is Jain against Sankhya, not between the two epics. On the Sankhya self the two accounts agree.

Kural 259 (அவிசொரிந்து ஆயிரம் வேட்டலின் ... உயிர்செகுத்து உண்ணாமை நன்று) ranks abstention above sacrifice, and Neelakesi 836 charges the sacrificers with the killing (கொலைகளும் இரங்கலிர்) and its heavy deed (அருவினை), even as eaters (அசிப்பவர்). That extends the couplet; it does not limit it, so develops fits better than qualifies. Both also turn on eating, which the note leaves out.

Neelakesi 140's உடம்பொடு வேறெனும் ஓர்ப்பு and Kural 340's துச்சில் இருந்த உயிர் share the idea of a self lodged apart from the body. But the couplet is a rhetorical question about impermanence (புக்கில் அமைந்தின்று), not a doubtful question awaiting a doctrine. Nothing in it explains endurance of torment, so both teaches and the epic-side gain are read in.

Neelakesi 296 fixes on the Buddhist the denial of space (ஆகாய நினக்கில்லை). The Buddhist teacher of Manimekalai 29 lets the example fail both for one who says ஆகாசம் அசத்து (381) and for one who says உண்டு (383), without taking a side. So the Buddhist text itself treats the reality of space as open, which qualifies the Jain attribution, and the note reports both ends accurately.

Kovalan's infatuation (விடுதல் அறியா விருப்பினன், 174) and Aravanar's teaching (பற்றின் வருவது முன்னது, 66) are tied by more than theme, since Madhavi brings Aravanar her lover's grief (காதலன் உற்ற கடுந் துயர், 63). Still, the teaching is about all the born (பிறந்தோர்), and the link only fits a doctrine to an earlier scene. The garland was sold by the doe-eyed woman (மான்அமர் நோக்கி), not certainly by Madhavi.

Kundalakesi 1 praises a lord who laboured only for others (பிறர்க்கே உறுதிக்கு உழந்தான்), and Neelakesi 222 mocks a monkey's self-offering as no greatness (கிடத்தல் தன் மாட்சியோ), so a real dispute over self-giving exists. But the Jain verse argues that limbs are for rising against killers (காலும் கையும் எழற்கு); it says nothing about saving no one or about results. The intention-against-result framing in note and teaches is not in the Tamil.

Kural 331 (நில்லாதவற்றை நிலையின என்றுணரும் புல்லறிவு) is a moral warning against trusting passing things. Neelakesi 377 is Mokkalan's technical dilemma about whether a lasting thing can act (நிலையுதல் ... கருமமும் காண்பரிது). The link joins them on the word நிலை and credits the couplet with a metaphysical assumption it does not make.
links.text_issue: Neelakesi 377 line 2 காயத்தின் றன்மைய is unclear.

links.reason: The patikam's thesis ஊழ்வினை உருத்துவந்து ஊட்டும் (0:57) is completed in the closing kaathai by an even law in which அறப்பயன் விளைதலும் மறப்பயன் விளைதலும் (30:138) and love carries one to rebirth (அற்புளஞ் சிறந்தோர் பற்றுவழிச் சேறலும், 137; Maadari reborn for love of Kannaki, 132-135). The frame really does turn karma's wrath into a law that also rewards. Only 'the mothers' overstates this unit, which shows one herdswoman.

Neelakesi 536 attacks the rule that gentle speech is a good deed (பையச் சொல்லுதல் நல்வினை) with soft-spoken plotters of killing. Kural 91 defines sweet speech as moist with love and free of deceit (ஈரம் அளைஇப் படிறிலவாம்), which excludes exactly that case. The pairing shows the couplet's clauses doing work, and both gains are true.

Kural 264 grants that தவம் can crush foes (ஒன்னார்த் தெறலும்) if one so intends. Neelakesi 49 has the sage resolve to make her understand her powerlessness (தெருட்டுவேன் இவள் திறமின்மை) and come to dharma (அறநெறி பெறுதலும்), but it never says he could destroy her and refrains. The 'power held back' in teaches and gains is read in; the closer fit, unmentioned, is the couplet's உவந்தாரை ஆக்கல்.

Manimekalai 30:40-41 (யானும் இன்றி என்னதும் இன்றி போனதும் இன்றி வந்ததும் இன்றி) denies a self in the chain, while granting that it goes on and does not wholly perish (பின்போக்கு அல்லது பொன்றக் கெடாதாய், 38). Neelakesi 201 argues that whatever carries over is a soul, like the thread in a garland (பெருந்தாமத்து உண்ணூல்போல் ... உயிர்). They are incompatible, and the shared ground teaches names is in the Tamil.

Both verses attack the same thesis, 256 by parody (சருவம் துக்கம்) and 556 by consequence: if there is no joy, stop counselling and keeping conduct and walk into fire (உறுதிகூறல் ஒழி ஒழுக்கம் காத்தல் ஒழி ... தீப்புகாய்). The pairing records a repeated attack in two tones, which is thin as a link. It answers or reverses nothing.

Kovalan's blame of the deceiver (சலம்புணர் கொள்கைச் சலதியொடு ஆடி, 69) and the narrator's வினைகடைக் கூட்ட (78) do set a conventional verdict against another cause. But Kural 920 calls double-minded women, drink and dice the company of those Fortune has already left (திருநீக்கப் பட்டார் தொடர்பு), a sign rather than a cause, so teaches misstates what the epic sets aside. Kovalan also applies it to Madhavi, not to himself as teaches says.

Both units turn on an old diviner's pronouncement of divinity: the பொய்யா மரபின் ஊர் முது வேலன் who says முருகு (Ainkurunuru 245), and the possessed மூதறிவாட்டி (தெய்வமுற்று, 50). Read together, the akam irony is reversed into prophecy. But the velan casts beads (கழங்கு) and is not possessed. Kannaki's பேதுறவு (51) is a shy bride's thought, not the akam scepticism the epic-side gain makes of it.

Purananuru 233 wishes false (பொய்யாகியரோ) the dawn report of wounds on Evvi, leader of the bards' families (இரும்பாண் ஒக்கல் தலைவன்). Akananuru 115 uses as a passing simile the bards who broke their lutes at the battle where Evvi fell (எவ்வி வீழ்ந்த செருவில் பாணர் ... வணர்மருப்பு). The pairing does show a death refused in puram become a known memory in akam.

The goddess's word that the meal the sage ate will not go idle (அவ் அறம் நின்னாங்கு ஒழியாது நின் பிறப்பு அறுத்திடும், 10:40-41) is answered when Manimekalai names the bowl that meal's fruit (ஆங்கு அதன் பயனே ... இப் பாத்திரம் என் கைப் புகுந்தது, 11:105-106). The fruit comes first as a means of feeding others, so teaches holds.

Kundalakesi 14's body where worms small and grown feed and live (சிறியவும் மூத்தவுமாகி நுனைய புழுக்குலம் ... வாழவும் பட்ட வினைய உடம்பு) and Neelakesi 360's many lives in the body (உடம்பினுள்ள பல்லுயிர் சாவ) are one image. One uses it to deny 'mine', the other to charge the bodhisattva's gift with killing. 'Disgust' slightly mislabels the Buddhist use, which argues against யான் எனது.

Both use the seed of virtue. Naladiyar 38's banyan seed grows great when it falls into worthy hands (தக்கார்கைப் பட்டக்கால்), and the goddess says the gift to the sage will not go idle and will cut births (41), yet calls Lakshmi herself a seed of dharma about to fall on burnt saline ground (கந்தசாலியின் ... வித்து ... வெங் களர் வீழ்வது, 46-48) through her clinging. The epic does add the giver's side and a different harvest.

Kural 353's ஐயம் is the seeker's doubt that bars release. Manimekalai's சங்கயம் (274) is the technical inconclusiveness of a reason that meets a contrary reason in debate. The link stretches a shared word, and the claim that clarity 'cannot come from matching proofs' is in neither text.

Kannaki's order to leave பார்ப்பார் அறவோர் பசு ... and go to தீத்திறத்தார் பக்கமே (21:53-55) is carried out when the flame spares அறவோர் மருங்கு, the cows and calves escape (கறவையும் கன்றும் கனலெரி சேரா), and fire crowds into மறவோர் சேரி (22:113-115). Command and fulfilment are named, and the அறவோர்/மறவோர் sorting supports teaches.
links.text_issue: Line 113 விடாது can be read either way; line 111 is doubted in the edition, though the link does not rest on it.

links.reason: Kural 355 (எப்பொருள் எத்தன்மைத் தாயினும் அப்பொருள் மெய்ப்பொருள் காண்பது) asks one to see the real thing whatever its outward nature, which points past appearances. Neelakesi 499 says nothing is known except through its qualities (குணமுகத்தாலன்றி). Making the couplet's 'whatever its nature' into the Jain method of reaching a thing through its qualities bends it toward the opposite sense.

Silappathikaram 6:7-13 explains the bhuta as Indra's gift to the king who guarded his city against the asuras, and that does deepen the altar rite of 5:63-80. But 5:65-66 already gives the reason (வெற்றிவேல் மன்னற்கு உற்றதை ஒழிக்க எனத் தேவர் கோமான் ஏவலின் போந்த), so the claim that the city's own rite does not explain it is false. What is left is close to adjacent narration.

Innaa Narpathu 31 (பண்ணமையா யாழின்கீழ்ப் பாடல் பெரிதின்னா) faults the tuning and Thirikadugam 57 (கொட்டி அளந்தமையாப் பாடல்) the beat, so the pitch/time distinction in teaches is in the words. But two lists of painful things agreeing that bad music is painful is thin. A view held by 'the period' is more than two verses show.

Neelakesi 304 gives உழப்பு அறிவு குறி செய்கை one owner (ஒருவனவே), against a Buddhist list of aggregates, so a real self/no-self opposition exists. But Manimekalai's terms are நுகர்ச்சி குறிப்பு பாவனை உள்ள அறிவு (189-190): only அறிவு and near-குறி match, so 'term for term' is false. The Manimekalai unit also only names the aggregates and does not itself deny an owner.

The goddess's saying that fire will eat Madurai and its king on a fixed day (ஆடித் திங்கள் ... ஒள்ளெரி யுண்ண உரைசால் மதுரையோடு அரைசுகேடுறும் எனும் உரையும் உண்டே, 23:133-137) supplies the backing for the fire god's unexplained standing order (பண்டேயோர் ஏவலுடையேன், 21:51-52). Together they make Kannaki's act the occasion of a fixed sentence, as teaches says.

ஊழ்வினை உருத்துவந்து ஊட்டும் (0:57) against சிவனருளால் வினை சேரகிலாமை is a defensible tension, and the note says which reading it depends on. But teaches' claim that the epic offers no grace that could stop the deed goes beyond the patikam unit. The epic's own goddess limits the failure of penance to செம்மையிலோர் (23:172), leaving room for its avail to the upright.

The venba's மாமகளும் நாமகளும் மாமயிடற் செற்றுகந்த கோமகளும் is pictured in the next kaathai's lotus in the left hand and sword in the right, half dark and half gold (23:5-8), so 'named then pictured' holds in part. நாமகள் has no counterpart in the portrait, and the two units are a venba and the kaathai that follows it, close to plain sequence.

The mantra of another form (வேற்று உரு எய்தவும் ஆக்கும் ... மந்திரம், 10:80-82) is used when Manimekalai sits in a man's form (ஆண்மைக் கோலத்து, 23:53), a real gift and use. But the goddess gives it because no one will tell a young girl the true doctrines (இளையள் வளையோள் என்று உனக்கு யாவரும் விளை பொருள் உரையார், 79-80), for hearing the schools, not as a defence against distrust. Calling this its first use is also doubtful.

Aravanar's deferral (ஆங்கு அவை நிகழ்ந்த பின்னர் அல்லது ... பொருளுரை பொருந்தாய், 12:106-107) is fulfilled when Manimekalai, having rejected the five schools (செவ்விது அன்மையின் சிந்தையின் வைத்திலேன், 29:44), asks அடிகள் மெய்ப்பொருள் அருளுக and he teaches. The later unit answers the earlier, as the note says.

Both close on the throbbing left eye with இடம் (இறந்துகண் ஆடும் இடம்; உண் கண்ணும் ஆடுமால், இடனே), so this is a shared omen and close rather than one poem developing the other. Two poems show only that the sign could end a poem. A 'recognised closing proof' is a modest generalisation.

Manimekalai's முயற்கோடு இன்மையின் தோற்றமும் இல் (30:216) and Mokkalan's hare and donkey with no horn (முயலும் கழுதைப் பெயர் பெற்றனவும் ... கோடு ... எழல் இல்லை) do share the example and its use for non-arising. But the hare's horn is a stock example of all the schools, and 'fairly reproduces Buddhist doctrine' rests on that single shared example.
links.text_issue: Neelakesi 404 line 1 lists கன்று, which is unexplained.

links.reason: Naladiyar 121's burning ground is a figure for the meat-eater's belly (புல்லறிவாளர் வயிறு). Neelakesi 32 describes a real cremation ground with demons that eat bodies (யாக்கை ... உண் பேய்க்கணம்) round a goddess's shrine, and says nothing of human flesh-eating. A shared setting is dressed up as the epic literalising the quatrain.

Kural 320 (நோயெல்லாம் நோய்செய்தார் மேலவாம்) and Neelakesi 587's turn of பிறர்க்கே உழந்தாய் into a charge (நீ உழப்பாய்) make a real hard case for the rule. But the verse works from the Buddhist's own definition (தீயுழப்பே செயும் தீவினை என்பது), and whether the pain is the giver's or that of those he gave away is unsettled (line 2 compressed). So teaches rests on an insecure reading.
links.text_issue: Neelakesi 587 line 2 வாயுழப்பாம் வழி is compressed.

links.reason: Line 15 அல்லலுற் றாற்றா தழுவாளை stands close to Kural 555's அல்லற்பட்டு ஆற்றாது அழுத கண்ணீர, and the note rightly calls it the same condition, not a quotation. The epic makes those tears the moment the city asks வளையாத செங்கோல் வளைந்தது இதுவென்கொல் (18), turning the couplet's slow wearing of wealth into a verdict on the king. Both gains hold.

Kannaki's Chola precedent of the gate bell (வாயிற் கடைமணி நடுநா நடுங்க, 20:63) is answered by the goddess's மறைநா ஓசை அல்லது யாவதும் மணிநா ஓசை கேட்டதும் இலனே (23:31-32). The later unit turns the earlier's proof into a counter-claim for the Pandya line, as teaches says.

The ancestor asks கொடுங்கோல் உண்டுகொல் and has it looked into (அறிந்தீமின், 23:111-112) while Vaarthikan is only imprisoned, owns the fault (என் இறைமுறை பிழைத்தது) and repairs it with villages. Nedunjeliyan learns only after the killing and can pay only with his life (யானே கள்வன் ... கெடுகவென் ஆயுள், 20:85-87). The difference teaches names, when the king inquires, is in the Tamil.
links.text_issue: Lines 121-122 of 23:103-122 are of unclear word division.

links.reason: In Tirumanthiram 1527 grace comes as guru (இன்னருட் சத்தி குருவென வந்து) and release follows when one's own doing ends (தன்செயல் அற்றால்). In Manimekalai 21:179 the disciple of the great one who gives dharma is saved by her own cutting (சார்பு அறுத்து உய்தி). That is a real incompatibility over who acts in release, the kind of grace-versus-effort tension this round tests, and both gains hold.

Teaches itself shows there is no tension: Kural 1 says only that the world has the primal Lord as first (ஆதி பகவன் முதற்றே உலகு), and Neelakesi 771's regress (தன்னைப் படைப்பின் ... முடிவில்லை) attacks a maker. By the link's own account the two are compatible. The pairing does sharpen first against creator, so it would stand as qualifies.
